about.sternocleidomastoid: Turns and bends the head and helps when you breathe hard.
about.scalenes: Tilt the neck to the side and lift the upper ribs as you breathe in.
about.splenius: Extends and turns the head and holds it up.
about.deltoid: Lifts the arm forward, to the side and back; it shapes the shoulder.
about.rotator-cuff: Four small muscles that keep the shoulder centred and rotate the arm.
about.pectoralis-major: Brings the arm across the body and pushes forward, as in a push-up.
about.pectoralis-minor: Pulls the shoulder blade forward and down.
about.serratus-anterior: Holds the shoulder blade against the ribs and turns it upward overhead.
about.trapezius: Lifts, squeezes and lowers the shoulder blades and supports the neck.
about.rhomboids: Squeeze the shoulder blades together, as in a row.
about.levator-scapulae: Lifts the shoulder blade and tilts the neck.
about.latissimus-dorsi: Pulls the arm down and back, as in a pull-up; the widest back muscle.
about.teres-major: Helps the lats pull the arm down and turn it inward.
about.erector-spinae: Straightens the spine and holds it upright when you lift or hinge.
about.multifidus: Small deep muscles that steady each vertebra.
about.quadratus-lumborum: Bends the trunk to the side and steadies the pelvis and lower back.
about.biceps-brachii: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
about.brachialis: The main elbow flexor, whichever way the palm faces.
about.triceps-brachii: Straightens the elbow, as in a press or a push-up.
about.brachioradialis: Bends the elbow with the thumb up, as in a hammer curl.
about.forearm-flexors: Bend the wrist and fingers and give you grip.
about.forearm-extensors: Straighten the wrist and fingers and balance the grip.
about.rectus-abdominis: Bends the trunk forward and braces the front of the core.
about.obliques: Twist and side-bend the trunk and resist rotation.
about.transversus-abdominis: The deepest abdominal muscle; it tightens the waist like a belt.
about.diaphragm: The main breathing muscle; it also helps brace the trunk under load.
about.glutes: Extend and open the hip and keep the pelvis level; key in squats and jumps.
about.hip-flexors: Lift the knee towards the chest and bend the trunk at the hip.
about.hip-rotators: Turn the thigh outward and keep the hip stable.
about.quadriceps: Straighten the knee; they drive squats, lunges and jumps.
about.hamstrings: Bend the knee and extend the hip, as in a deadlift.
about.adductors: Bring the legs together and help the hip in deep squats.
about.calves: Lift the heel; they push off when you run and jump.
about.tibialis-anterior: Lifts the toes and controls the foot as it lands.
about.fibularis: Turns the sole outward and steadies the ankle.

SiteInfo.whatIsAnswer: Palee is a training platform for gyms, coaches and athletes. It brings class scheduling and booking, personalised programming, live workout execution, coaching conversations and progress tracking into one app.
SiteInfo.whoForAnswer: Gym owners and staff who run classes, coaches who program for athletes, and members who book classes and log their training.
SiteInfo.offlineAnswer: Yes. A workout keeps running without a connection: check-offs are saved on the device and sync when the connection returns.
SiteInfo.adsAnswer: No. Palee shows no ads and does not track members for advertising. Training progress belongs to the athlete.
SiteInfo.languagesAnswer: English, Greek, Arabic, Russian, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Hebrew, Italian, Bulgarian, Dutch and French.
SiteInfo.twoSidesQuestion: Is Palee for gyms or for individual people?
SiteInfo.twoSidesAnswer: Both. Palee has two sides in one app: a business side where gyms, studios and independent coaches run classes, members, coaching and finance, and a social side where anyone, with or without a gym, keeps a training journal, joins clubs, finds training partners and goes to events.
SiteInfo.twoSidesSummary: Palee has two sides in one app: a business side where gyms, studios and independent coaches run classes, members, coaching and finance, and a social side where anyone, with or without a gym, keeps a training journal, joins clubs, finds training partners and goes to events.
SiteInfo.eventsQuestion: Can I organise events with Palee?
SiteInfo.eventsAnswer: Yes. Gyms, coaches, clubs and individual organisers can publish events such as open WODs, bootcamps, runs and competitions, with capacity, waitlist, guest passes, co-hosts and an organiser console for management, finances and analytics. Nearby events appear in Around me.
SiteInfo.socialSummary: A feed of your clubs and the people you follow, club channels, posts with photos and workouts, and Around me to discover nearby events, open clubs and gyms on a map.
SiteInfo.partnersSummary: Find a training partner among verified members of your own club with mutual opt-in, and pick a support buddy who hears from you only when you ask for help.
SiteInfo.eventsSummary: Open WODs, bootcamps, runs and competitions with RSVPs, capacity, waitlist, guest passes, co-hosting and an organiser console for management, finances and analytics.
SiteInfo.boxSummary: Book classes and appointments, check in with a rotating QR code, a Wallet pass or NFC, see today's workout, follow your packages and pay, all from one Box tab.
SiteInfo.trainingSummary: Run any workout with a step-synchronised timer, scaling options, per-exercise notes, injury warnings and offline check-offs, or log a score in seconds, even by voice.
SiteInfo.journalSummary: Every workout, PR, note and rating in one journal that belongs to the athlete and follows them across gyms and coaches, private by default with a clear visibility ladder.
SiteInfo.bodySummary: Body measurements and progress photos with a pose guide and compare slider, plus water, sleep, meals, mood and cravings, with health-safe defaults such as showing weight as a trend only.
SiteInfo.progressSummary: Consistency, strength, benchmarks, muscle coverage on a 3D anatomy atlas, the ten fitness qualities, training load and insights such as sleep versus performance.
SiteInfo.businessSummary: Class schedules and series, appointments, check-in desk, workout library with goals, challenges, community moderation, inventory, cleaning log, reviews and reports.
SiteInfo.coachingSummary: Programs, reply and form-review queues, nutrition plans, coach notes, PT squads and session packages; independent coaches get their own lighter console and a team club.
SiteInfo.financeSummary: Packages and seasons, promotions, member billing, invoices and refunds, corporate clients, reconciliation and accounting exports.
SiteInfo.growthSummary: A public gym page, owner-controlled trial slots, member referrals with rewards and open events bring new clients while the relationship stays with the gym.
SiteInfo.branchesSummary: Staff roles and permissions scoped to branches, a branch filter across finance, coaching and statistics, and one-step creation of classes or packages for several branches.
SiteInfo.devicesSummary: An installable web app that works offline, native iOS and Android builds, Garmin, Apple Health and Health Connect, home-screen widgets, calendar feeds and push notifications.
SiteInfo.privacySummary: No ads, private-by-default data, report and block tools, data export, each gym in its own time zone, and the whole app in twelve languages.
